'''Dennis Gail Peters''' (April 17, 1937 – April 13, 2020) was an American analytical chemist who specialized in [[electrochemistry]] and was named the [[Herman T. Briscoe]] Professor at [[Indiana University]] in 1975. Peters led his own research group at Indiana University in [[Bloomington, Indiana]] until his death in 2020. Peters' research focused on the electrochemical behavior of halogenated organic compounds, more recently moving to focus on transition metal catalysts in regards to the oxidation and reduction of organic species.<ref name="Peters Group Dr. Peters">{{cite web |title=Peters Group Dr. Dennis G. Peters |url=http://www.indiana.edu/~echem/index.php?page=drpeters |website=Indiana University Bloomington |accessdate=1 November 2018 |ref=1 |archive-date=September 30, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120930193626/http://www.indiana.edu/~echem/index.php?page=drpeters |url-status=dead }}</ref> He authored or co-authored over 210 publications and 5 analytical chemistry textbooks.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Eckelbarger |first1=Emily |title=IU Professor Named American Chemical Society Fellow |url=https://www.idsnews.com/article/2017/07/iu-professor-named-american-chemical-society-fellow |accessdate=2 November 2018 |publisher=Indiana Daily Student |date=July 19, 2017}}</ref>

==Early life and education==
Dennis Peters was born on April 17, 1937, in [[Los Angeles, California]]. He completed his Bachelor of Science in chemistry from the [[California Institute of Technology]] in 1958 and graduated [[cum laude]] before completing his PhD in analytical chemistry at [[Harvard University]] under James J. Lingane.<ref name="thesis-peters-1962">{{cite thesis |url=https://www.proquest.com/docview/302091593 |title=Chronopotentiometric studies with platinum and gold electrodes |date=1962 |publisher=[[Harvard University]] |degree=Ph.D. |last=Peters |first=Dennis Gail |url-access=subscription  |oclc=1035219754 |id={{ProQuest|302091593}} }}</ref> After completing his PhD in 1962, Peters went to [[Indiana University]] in [[Bloomington, Indiana]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Indiana University Chemistry Department Faculty Dennis Peters |url=http://www.chem.indiana.edu/faculty/dennis-peters/ |website=Indiana University Bloomington Department of Chemistry |accessdate=1 November 2018}}</ref>

==Career==
Peters served as the chemistry department's graduate student advisor from 1969 to 1971 where he recruited the department's largest incoming class.<ref>{{cite web |title=Scientist at Work: Dennis Peters |url=http://newsinfo.iu.edu/web/page/normal/16019.html |website=IU News Room |accessdate=2 November 2018}}</ref> His research has focused on the mechanistic and synthetic properties of the oxidation and reduction of halogenated organic compounds and electrocatalysis in organic synthesis.<ref>{{cite web |title=Dennis Gail Peters Honors and Awards |url=https://honorsandawards.iu.edu/search-awards/honoree.shtml?honoreeID=1952 |website=IU University Honors & Awards |accessdate=2 November 2018 |archive-date=November 30, 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181130030506/https://honorsandawards.iu.edu/search-awards/honoree.shtml?honoreeID=1952 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Peters was still actively teaching up to the time he suffered a fall during spring break 2020 and was taken to a hospital.<ref name="ids-2020apr14" />

==Death==
Peters died from [[hospital-acquired]] [[COVID-19]] on April 13, 2020, four days before his 83rd birthday.<ref>{{cite web |title=In memory of Prof. Dennis G. Peters 1937-2020 |url=https://www.chem.indiana.edu/2020/04/in-memory-of-prof-dennis-g-peters-1937-2020/ |website=Indiana University Department of Chemistry |accessdate=16 April 2020 |date=14 April 2020}}</ref><ref name="wfiu-2020apr14">{{cite news |url=https://indianapublicmedia.org/news/iu-confirms-death-of-longtime-chemistry-professor-dennis-peters.php |title=IU Confirms Death Of Longtime Chemistry Professor Dennis Peters |website=[[WFIU]] |date=April 14, 2020 |first=Emma |last=Atkinson |archive-date=April 27, 2020 |access-date=April 17, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200427033706/https://indianapublicmedia.org/news/iu-confirms-death-of-longtime-chemistry-professor-dennis-peters.php |url-status=dead }}</ref> He contracted the virus while in a Bloomington hospital recovering from a fall.<ref name="ids-2020apr14">{{cite news |url=https://www.idsnews.com/article/2020/04/iu-chemistry-professor-dennis-peters-dies-from-complications-of-covid-19 |title=IU chemistry professor Dennis Peters dies from complications of COVID-19 |newspaper=[[Indiana Daily Student]] |date=April 14, 2020 |first=Shelby |last=Anderson}}</ref>

Peters' name was included in the May 2020 ''New York Times'' tribute ''[[U.S. Deaths Near 100,000, An Incalculable Loss]]'' to the 100,000 Americans who lost their lives as a direct result of the pandemic.<ref name="nyt-2020may24">{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2020/05/24/us/us-coronavirus-deaths-100000.html |title=U.S. Deaths Near 100,000, an Incalculable Loss |newspaper=[[New York Times]] |date=May 24, 2020 |page=A.1 |edition=Late (East Coast) |last=Barry |first=Dan |id={{ProQuest|2405964358}}}}</ref> A reporter for the ''[[Indiana Daily Student]]'' wrote that "Peters had a roaring voice that filled lecture halls".<ref name="ids-2020apr19">{{cite news |url=https://www.idsnews.com/article/2020/04/theres-a-void-in-the-world-students-staff-remember-iu-professor-dennis-peters |title='There's a void in the world': Students, staff remember IU professor Dennis Peters |newspaper=[[Indiana Daily Student]] |date=April 19, 2020 |first=Joey |last=Bowling}}</ref>

* 2012, Elected Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]<ref>{{cite web |title=AAAS Elected Fellows |url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/listing |website=AAAS |accessdate=2 November 2018}}</ref>
* 2017, Elected Fellow of the [[American Chemical Society]]<ref>{{cite web |title=2017 ACS Fellows |url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/fellows/list-of-2017-acs-fellows.html |website=ACS |accessdate=2 November 2018}}</ref>

Hirsch Award for Distinguished Service in the Advancement of Analytical Chemistry |date=February 19, 2020 |work=Indiana University}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://acsanalytical.org/awards-resources/national-acs-awards/acs-measurement-science-lectureships/ |title=The Roland F. Hirsch Award for Distinguished Service |work=ACS Division of Analytical Chemistry|date=April 4, 2019 }}</ref>
